AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  MARCH 17, 2020
REGULAR MEETING
  6:00 PM
  NORWALK CITY HALL/COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  AND VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE

  Margarita L. Rios, Mayor
  Luigi Vernola, Vice Mayor
  Tony Ayala, Councilmember
  Jennifer Perez, Councilmember
  Leonard Shryock, Councilmember
 Public Comment: Comments may be made in person, submitted via email at: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, or through
 the video conference during the designated time on any item on the agenda or on any other matter within the jurisdiction
 subject to the rules of decorum described in Norwalk Municipal Code §2.08.020. The maximum time allowed is three
 minutes.

 Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
 certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
 matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

 Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Council:

  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

 Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
 meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk's Department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening
 devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and
 documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
 Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
 that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

 Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it
 has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

 Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk's Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard
 during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday - Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday;
 telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

  STUDY SESSION MEETING – 5:00 p.m.

  TEMPORARY PUBLIC COMMENT EMAIL ESTABLISHED FOR CITY OF NORWALK CITY COUNCIL
  MEETINGS. EMAILS MUST BE RECEIVED BY 6 P.M. ON THE EVENING OF THE MEETING. CITY EMAIL:
  publiccomments@norwalkca.gov

CALL TO ORDER
   Mayor Rios

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FOR CLOSED SESSION MATTERS

CLOSED SESSION

  I.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNCIL PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54957: THREAT
  TO PUBLIC SERVICES OR FACILITIES – Consultation with the City Manager, Los Angeles County
  Sheriff representative, and other related City officials.

  II.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNCIL PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54856.9(d)(1):
  Kessner v. City of Santa Clara, et al., including the City of Norwalk; Superior Court Case No.
  20CV364054.

  III.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  §54956.8: Assessor Parcel Number 8045-008-902; Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus M. Gomez,
  City Manager; Negotiating Party: State of California; Under Negotiation: Price and Terms of Payment.

  IV.  PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE EVALUATION PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  §54957: City Manager.

RECESS

  REGULAR MEETING – 6:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Rios

INVOCATION
  Pastor Ruben Sandoval
  New Harvest Church

FLAG SALUTE
  Stany Hernandez, 9th grade
  John Glenn High School

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

  a.  Report of City Council Travel

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS - None

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS

  1.  Norwalk Baseball League Opening Day Highlights.

  2.  First Responders Luncheon Highlights.

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

CONSENT CALENDAR

Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call vote.
Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.

  1.  MEETING MINUTES – Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meetings of
  February 18 and March 9, 2020. 825-04

  Minutes
 2.  PAYROLL – Staff recommends City Council approve the payroll for the periods January 26, 2020 –
  February 8, 2020, in the amount of $948,803.38 and February 9, 2020 – February 22, 2020, in the
  amount of $942,524.27. 630

  Report

3.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS – Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant register periods of
  February 12 - 25, 2020, in the total amount of $3,142,984.39 and February 26 – March 10, 2020, in the
  total amount of $1,977,483.32. 640

  Report

4.  CLAIM AGAINST THE CITY – Staff recommends City Council deny the claim filed by Kimberly Slater.
  830-19

  Report

5.  PLANNING COMMISSION SYNOPSIS – MARCH 11, 2020 - No action is required unless the City
  Council elects to review the decision of the Planning Commission on those items where the
  Commission’s action was final. 320

  Synopsis

6.  PURCHASE AGREEMENT – FOUR ZERO EMISSION BATTERY ELECTRIC BUSES – Staff
  recommends City Council approve an agreement with Gillig, LLC to acquire four (4) zero emission
  battery electric buses in the amount of $3,881,586.40; and authorize the City Manager to execute the
  agreement and any amendments provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a
  form approved by the City Attorney. 634-03

  Report

7.  RESOLUTION NO. 20-15 – EXECUTION OF THE CALIFORNIA LOW CARBON TRANSIT
  OPERATIONS PROGRAM (LCTOP) – Staff recommends City Council adopt Resolution No. 20-15, A
  RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK AUTHORIZING THE
  EXECUTION OF THE LOW CARBON TRANSIT OPERATIONS PROGRAM PROJECT, in the amount
  of $118,696. 1105-02

  Report

8.  ACCEPTANCE OF WORK - HEATING, VENTILATION, AND AIR CONDITIONING (HVAC)
  REPLACEMENTS FOR TEEN CENTER, AQUATIC PAVILION, AND SOCIAL SERVICES CENTER -
  Staff recommends City Council accept the work of Tri-West Mechanical, Inc. for the installation of new
  heating, ventilation, and air conditioning units at the Teen Center, Aquatic Pavilion, and Social Services
  Center; and approve emergency replacement of two additional HVAC units installed at City Hall for
  Public Safety and MIS rooms. 1005-04-7796

  Report

9.  FEDERAL TRANSIT ADMINISTRATION CERTIFICATIONS AND ASSURANCES FOR FEDERAL
  FISCAL YEAR 2020 - Staff recommends City Council authorize the Executive Director of Regional
  Transportation to execute the Fiscal Year 2020 Certifications and Assurances FTA Assistance
  Programs/Affirmation of Applicant, file grant application(s) on behalf of the City and execute a grant
  agreement(s); in concurrence with and execution of the Affirmation of Applicant’s Attorney Certification
  by the City Attorney. 1105-01

  Report

10. THE 2019 NORWALK GENERAL PLAN AND HOUSING ELEMENT ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORT –
  Staff recommends City Council receive and file the 2019 General Plan and Housing Element Annual
  Progress Report, and direct staff to forward a copy of the report to the Governor’s Office of Planning
  and Research and the State Department of Housing and Community Development prior to April 1,
  2020. 320-02
   Report

  11. RESOLUTION NO. 20-16 – AMENDING FISCAL YEAR 2019/20 SALARY SCHEDULE – Staff
  recommends City Council adopt Resolution No. 20-16, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF
  THE CITY OF NORWALK AMENDING THE SALARY SCHEDULE FOR FISCAL YEAR 2019/20 FOR
  THE GENERAL, HOURLY, AND EXECUTIVE MANAGEMENT AND MID-MANAGEMENT UNIT
  EMPLOYEES. 135-03

  Report

  12. AGREEMENT AMENDMENT NO. 2 - EDUCATIONAL OUTREACH FOR MEASURE P, NORWALK
  ESSENTIAL SERVICES AND PUBLIC SAFETY MEASURE – Staff recommends City Council approve
  Amendment No. 2 to the agreement with Cerrell Associates Inc., increasing the total amount from
  $30,000 to $72,960; and authorize the City Manager to execute the amendment, on behalf of the City,
  in a form approved by the City Attorney.

  Report

APPOINTMENTS

  13. ADVISORY BODIES – Staff recommends City Councilmembers either re-appoint current Advisory
  Body members or make new appointments for two-year terms expiring on March 31, 2020. 200

  Report

REPORTS

  14. RESOLUTION NO. 20-17 – BUDGET AMENDMENT – AWARD OF CONTRACT - ADMINSTRATION
  SERVICES FOR FEDERALLY FUNDED PROJECTS – Staff recommends City Council:

  a.  adopt Resolution No. 20-17, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK AUTHORIZING AN AMENDMENT TO THE FISCAL YEAR 2019/20 ADOPTED
  BUDGET TO APPROPRIATE MEASURE R FUNDS FOR FUNDING ADMININSTRATION
  SERVICES FOR FEDERALLY FUNDED PRPOJECTS, in the amount of $201,139; and

  b.  approve a professional services agreement with Avant-Garde to provide funding administration
  services in the amount of $201,138.75, for the Federally funded projects as listed in Attachment
  No. 3; and authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement and any amendments provided
  there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 610

  Report

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

ADJOURNMENT

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted
on the City Hall bulletin board not less than 72 hours prior to the meeting. Dated March 13, 2020.

Theresa Devoy, CMC
City Clerk
